claims.text: The initial material is as-cast HfMoTaTiZr.
Mo should be substituted with a lighter refractory metal such as Ti.
Replacing Mo with a lighter refractory element will reduce the alloy's density.
The substitution will maintain strong room-temperature mechanical performance.
The substitution will maintain strong high-temperature mechanical performance.
Retention of a favorable microstructure could preserve mechanical properties after substitution.
The inherent properties of the selected refractory replacement could help preserve mechanical performance.
The substituted alloy is predicted to have approximately 5–10% lower density than the as-cast baseline.
The substituted alloy is predicted to avoid a significant loss of yield strength and fracture toughness.
As-cast HfMoTaTiZr has a density of 10.21 g cm−3.
As-cast HfMoTaTiZr has a room-temperature yield strength of approximately 1600 MPa.
As-cast HfMoTaTiZr has a high-temperature yield strength of 855 MPa.
The hypothesis is intended to apply from room temperature through 1600 °C.
A density reduction below 5%, a room-temperature yield-strength loss above 10%, or a 1000 °C yield-strength loss above 15% would falsify the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The stated temperature boundary extends to 1600 °C, but the controlled experiment specifies high-temperature yield-strength testing only at 1000 °C.

The predicted outcome requires preservation of fracture toughness, but the falsification rule contains no quantitative fracture-toughness rejection criterion; a severe toughness loss could therefore occur without triggering rejection.
